Lab confirmation of previous dengue infection is encoded as uncomputable. No vocabulary concept exists for it, and outside or prior lab results may not be reliably structured in the EHR.

Residence in an endemic area is encoded as uncomputable. Listed areas: Puerto Rico, American Samoa, US Virgin Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Republic of Marshall Islands, Republic of Palau. Updated endemic-area guidance and pre-vaccination laboratory testing guidance are referenced externally (CDC MMWR rr7006a1, cdc.gov/dengue/hcp/vaccine) and not represented.

Negative recommendation not encoded as a rule: 'Dengue vaccine should not be administered to children traveling to or visiting endemic dengue areas.' The residence requirement in the denominator partly reflects it.
Dosing schedule not represented: the 0, 6, and 12 month intervals, minimum intervals between doses, and minimum age of 9 years per dose.

Timing caveat: the series spans 12 months, so a child who turns 9 or starts the series late in the measurement year cannot yet have 3 doses. The rule does not model series-in-progress or catch-up logic. Human reviewer should consider this.
Rule contains derived parameters and uncomputable denominator criteria, so the engine will report it as largely not computable and it requires human review.
